chunks: From him, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Wahb, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
Qunut is in the Friday prayer, the maghrib prayer, the 'atamah prayer, the witr, and the morning prayer. So whoever abandons the qunut out of aversion to it, then there is no salat (prayer) for him.

key_terms.رَغْبَةً عَنْهُ: out of aversion or deliberate disinclination toward it
key_terms.فَلَا صَلَاةَ لَهُ: then there is no salat (prayer) for him
key_terms.ٱلْعِشَاءِ: the evening prayer referred to here
key_terms.ٱلْقُنُوتُ: the supplicatory standing or invocation performed in prayer

ai.seo_question: In which prayers is qunut prescribed, and what is the ruling on abandoning it out of aversion?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the prescribed place of qunut in several prayers and strongly emphasizes adherence to this sunnah (prophetic tradition). It indicates that abandoning qunut out of dislike for it is a grave matter affecting the validity or acceptance of one’s salat (prayer).
